Best open-ear earbuds for running (2026)

Based on the search results you provided, the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds are the best overall pick, while the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 are my top recommendation for dedicated runners. If value is your priority, consider the Soundcore AeroFit 2.

Top picks at a glance
Best overall
1. Bose Ultra Open Earbuds
$199

Runner’s World names these its best overall open-ear headphones. They offer excellent audio quality, a comfortable clip-on design, easy controls, and multipoint device switching.

Best for: Runners who want premium sound and everyday versatility.

Source: Runner’s World review.

 Buy at Bose · Compare at Amazon

Best for serious runners
2. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
$125 sale price cited

Combines bone conduction and directional air conduction for fuller sound without plugging your ears. The secure neckband design is made for workouts, and it has an IP55 rating.

Best for: Road running, long training sessions, and runners who prefer a stable fit.

Trade-off: It is less suitable for swimming than some other Shokz models.

Source: WIRED review.

 Buy at Amazon · Check REI

Best value
3. Soundcore AeroFit 2
$104 with code AFSC20*

Adjustable ear hooks, IP55 protection, up to 10 hours of earbud battery life and 42 hours with the case. The open design helps you stay aware of traffic.

Best for: Budget-conscious runners who want long battery life and adjustable fit.

The supplied deal listing reports that code AFSC20 was tested successfully on October 22, 2026, at Soundcore's store. Price and code acceptance can change.

Sources: Deal and specifications · SoundGuys review roundup.

 Buy at Soundcore with the supplied deal link · Compare at Amazon

4. Shokz OpenDots 2
$200

WIRED's overall open-ear pick, with up to 10 hours per charge and 40 hours total with the case. Its clip-on design leaves the top of the ear free for glasses, hats, and sunglasses.

Best for: Runners who want a compact, versatile clip-on design with strong water and dust resistance (IP57).

Source: WIRED's 2026 guide.

 Buy at Amazon · Buy at Shokz

5. JLab Flex Open
Budget pick

Runner’s World names these its best budget open-ear headphones. They're worth considering if you want to keep your spending down while retaining awareness of your surroundings.

Best for: Casual runners and shoppers who prioritize price over premium features.

Source: Runner’s World recommendations.

My recommendation: Choose the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 if running is your main use. Choose the Soundcore AeroFit 2 if you prefer conventional ear-hook earbuds and want to spend less. For premium audio and everyday wear, go with the Bose.

One important safety note: open-ear headphones help you hear your surroundings, but they don't guarantee that you'll notice approaching vehicles or cyclists. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic, particularly when running outdoors.
